# Scoped Re-Review Prompt Template

Use this template when dispatching a re-review after a fix round. The
re-reviewer verifies the findings were addressed or declined with
confirmed evidence and checks the fix diff for new breakage. It is not a
fresh review — the full review already happened.

**Purpose:** Verify each finding from the previous review was addressed or
declined with confirmed evidence, and that the fix itself broke nothing.

```
Subagent (general-purpose):
  description: "Re-review Task N fix round R"
  model: [MODEL — REQUIRED: choose per SKILL.md Model Selection; an omitted
         model silently inherits the session's most expensive one]
  run_in_background: false   # Claude Code: dispatch in the foreground (SKILL.md "Waiting on subagents"); omit on harnesses without the flag
  prompt: |
    You are re-reviewing one task's fix round. A previous review produced
    findings; an implementer has attempted to fix them. Your job is to
    verdict each finding and inspect the fix diff — nothing else.

    ## The Task

    Read the task brief: [BRIEF_FILE]

    ## The Findings Under Verification

    [FINDINGS]

    ## The Fix

    Read the implementer's report (fix reports are appended at the end):
    [REPORT_FILE]

    **Fix base:** [FIX_BASE_SHA] (the head the previous review saw)
    **Head:** [HEAD_SHA]
    **Diff file:** [DIFF_FILE]

    Read the diff file once — it contains the fix commits, a stat summary,
    and the fix diff with surrounding context. Do not re-run git commands.
    If the diff file is missing, fetch the diff yourself:
    `git diff --stat [FIX_BASE_SHA]..[HEAD_SHA]` and
    `git diff [FIX_BASE_SHA]..[HEAD_SHA]`.

    An all-declined round has no fix diff: the diff file above is then the
    previous review's package, and every finding's evidence lives in code that
    diff did not change. Read the cited file:line for each declined finding
    directly; nothing in this round is "outside the fix diff".

    Your review is read-only on this checkout. Do not mutate the working
    tree, the index, HEAD, or branch state in any way. Use tools like
    `git show`, `git diff`, and `git log` to inspect history. If you need a
    working copy of a different revision, check it out into a separate
    temporary directory (e.g. `git worktree add /tmp/review-[SHA] [SHA]`) —
    never move HEAD on this checkout.

    ## You Do Not Dispatch Subagents

    Do all of this review yourself. Never spawn a subagent to review part
    of the diff, and never spawn another reviewer for a second opinion.
    This process already provides every review seat the work gets; a
    reviewer you spawn duplicates one of them at full cost, and its
    verdict counts for nothing. If the diff feels too large for one
    pass, review it in passes yourself and say so in your report.

    ## Scope

    Your scope is the findings list and the fix diff. Verdict every finding.
    Inspect the fix diff for new problems the fix itself introduced. Do NOT
    re-review code the fix did not touch: if you notice an issue entirely
    outside the fix diff, report it under Out-of-Scope Observations — it
    does not block this task and does not extend the loop. A broad
    whole-branch review happens after all tasks are complete. When the round
    declined a finding, the cited code is in scope whether or not the diff
    touched it.

    ## Tests

    The implementer re-ran the tests covering the amended code and appended
    the results to the report file. Treat the report as unverified claims:
    confirm the fix report names the covering tests and shows their output,
    and verify the claims against the diff. That requirement covers the
    findings the round fixed; a declined finding is confirmed from its
    file:line evidence, not from tests. Do not re-run the suite to confirm
    their report. Run a test only when reading the code raises a specific
    doubt that no existing run answers — and then a focused test, never a
    package-wide suite.

    ## Output Format

    Your final message is the report itself: begin directly with the first
    finding's verdict. Every line is a verdict, a finding with file:line,
    or a check you ran — no preamble, no process narration.

    ### Finding Verdicts

    For each finding in The Findings Under Verification, in order:
    - **[finding one-liner]** — ADDRESSED | NOT ADDRESSED | DECLINED, with file:line
      evidence. "Attempted" is not addressed: the specific defect must no
      longer exist.
    - DECLINED means the implementer refuted the finding (the cited code
      does not do what it says) or corrected it (real, but not blocking
      severity or not this change's scope) with file:line evidence you have
      read and confirmed. A decline whose evidence you cannot confirm is
      NOT ADDRESSED and stays open.

    ### New Breakage in the Fix Diff

    Anything the fix itself broke or introduced, with severity
    (Critical/Important/Minor) and file:line. "None" if clean.

    ### Out-of-Scope Observations

    Issues you noticed entirely outside the fix diff. Non-blocking; the
    controller ledgers these for the final review. "None" if none.

    ### Verdict

    **Fix round:** [All findings addressed or declined, no new
    Critical/Important breakage | Findings remain open] — list the open
    ones.
```

**Placeholders:**
- `[MODEL]` — REQUIRED: reviewer model per SKILL.md Model Selection; scoped
  re-reviews of small fix diffs take a cheap-to-mid tier
- `[BRIEF_FILE]` — the task brief file (same file the implementer worked from)
- `[FINDINGS]` — the Critical/Important findings and spec gaps from the
  previous review, copied verbatim, one per bullet
- `[REPORT_FILE]` — the implementer's report file (fix reports appended)
- `[FIX_BASE_SHA]` — the head the previous review saw
- `[HEAD_SHA]` — current commit
- `[DIFF_FILE]` — the path from `scripts/review-package PLAN_FILE FIX_BASE HEAD`'s `wrote <path>: ...` line

The read-only clause inside the prompt is a verbatim copy of
[reviewer-read-only-clause.md](../requesting-code-review/reviewer-read-only-clause.md),
the single source for every reviewer template; `tests/sdd/test-sdd-contract.sh`
fails when any copy drifts from it. Change the source file and re-copy — never
edit a copy in place.

**Final-wave usage:** this same template covers the fix wave of the FINAL
whole-branch review, where the findings span tasks and no task brief exists.
There `[BRIEF_FILE]` carries the plan file, `[FINDINGS]` carries the final
review's findings list, and the description reads "Re-review final fix wave".
The reviewer verdicts those branch-level findings against the fix diff exactly
as the template above specifies — its "one task's fix round" framing does not
narrow the scope in that usage.

**Carve-out usage (controller-applied de-minimis fixes):** when the fix
round was controller-applied under SKILL.md's de-minimis exception, read
"the implementer" in this prompt as the controller: the fix report and
covering-command output land in the same task report file, and your job
is unchanged — verify the named findings against the diff.

**Re-reviewer returns:** per-finding verdicts (ADDRESSED / NOT ADDRESSED / DECLINED),
new breakage in the fix diff, out-of-scope observations, and a round verdict.

## Fix round 1

**Finding:** TERMINATOR_PATTERN (line 39) and endsWithAbbreviation regex (line 46) contained ASCII quotes `"'"` instead of the typographic quotes from the brief: U+201D ", U+2019 ', U+201C ", U+2018 '. This caused sentences with curly-quoted dialogue to be undercounted.

**Disposition:** Real. Verified:
- `sentenceCount("Go." Then left.)` returned 1 instead of 2
- Current code has ASCII `22 27` (ASCII quotes), brief requires UTF-8 `e2809d e28099` (U+201D U+2019) in TERMINATOR_PATTERN

**Test added:** test/sentenceCount.test.js line 70: `'handles curly-quoted dialogue correctly'` with input `'He said "Go." Then left.'` expecting 2 sentences

**Command:** `npm test`

**RED output (before fix):** Expected 2, actual 1 for curly-quoted test
**GREEN output (after fix):**
```
ℹ tests 26
ℹ pass 26
ℹ fail 0
```

**Files changed:**
- src/textstats.js: line 39 (TERMINATOR_PATTERN), line 46 (endsWithAbbreviation regex)
- test/sentenceCount.test.js: added curly-quoted dialogue test

**Commit:** aef2cc6 fix: restore typographic quotes in sentenceCount regexes

1	---
2	name: subagent-driven-development
3	description: Use when executing implementation plans with independent tasks in the current session
4	---
5	
6	# Subagent-Driven Development
7	
8	Execute plan by dispatching a fresh implementer subagent per task, a task review (spec compliance + code quality) after each, and a broad whole-branch review at the end.
9	
10	**Why subagents:** You delegate tasks to specialized agents with isolated context. By precisely crafting their instructions and context, you ensure they stay focused and succeed at their task. They should never inherit your session's context or history — you construct exactly what they need. This also preserves your own context for coordination work.
11	
12	**Core principle:** Fresh subagent per task + task review (spec + quality) + broad final review = high quality, fast iteration
13	
14	**Narration:** between tool calls, narrate at most one short line — the
15	ledger and the tool results carry the record.
16	
17	**REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use hyperpowers:communication for anything you write to your human partner in this skill: the pre-flight question, an escalation, a BLOCKED hand-back.
18	
19	**Continuous execution:** Do not pause to check in with your human partner between tasks. Execute all tasks from the plan without stopping. While the plan has tasks left, a turn ends in exactly three cases: a BLOCKED status you cannot resolve; a question only your human partner can answer, asked in that message (ambiguity that genuinely prevents progress is such a question); or, on a harness that cannot wait in the foreground, tracked work still running, named in that message. A message that names your next step is followed by that step's tool call in the same turn. "Tasks 1 and 2 are done. Moving to Task 3." followed by a turn end is a stop: your human partner reads it as work in progress, and nothing resumes it until they type. Completing the last task does not end the plan: it opens the final whole-branch review, and the plan ends only after Finish. Each permitted turn end, and "your human partner asked you to stop", is written to the ledger in the same message that ends the turn: run `scripts/sdd-state handback PLAN_FILE --reason "<why>"` (add `--session <sid>` on a harness without `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`; `busy` or `error` is retried, and without the line the guard falls back to reading your last message). Write that line only for a question only your human partner can answer, a BLOCKED report, or their request to stop; finishing the tasks is never a reason for it. On Claude Code the SDD stop guard refuses a turn end it can prove is premature, two consecutive attempts per plan, the count resetting after any allow, with this message: "SDD stop guard: plan <plan path> is not finished (<state>; nothing tracked is live). Take the next step now, in this turn. If you are handing back to your human partner (a question only they can answer, a BLOCKED report, or they asked you to stop), run scripts/sdd-state handback PLAN_FILE --session <sid> --reason "<why>" and end the turn with that message." (with a live job the first sentences name the job and say to watch it with `tracked-job wait`). When you meet it, take the next step; writing a question you do not need answered to get past it is the stop it exists to prevent, and the log records every allow. "Should I continue?" prompts and progress summaries waste their time — they asked you to execute the plan, so execute it.
20	
21	**Tracked work only:** anything that outlives one tool call starts through your harness's tracked background option (`run_in_background` on Claude Code); never start it with a trailing `&`, `nohup`, `setsid`, `disown`, or a script that detaches a process. The harness never reports on such a process, so nothing wakes you when it ends, and a turn you end to wait for it does not resume.
22	
23	**After every context compaction:** this file fits within the 20,000 characters Claude Code re-attaches, so the copy you hold is whole. A step file you read before the compaction does not survive it. Before your next action, print the board and the ledger lines the step table names (your task's and your Setup's, never the whole ledger), find your step in the table, and Read that step file in full.
24	
25	## When to Use
26	
27	```dot
28	digraph when_to_use {
29	    "Have implementation plan?" [shape=diamond];
30	    "Tasks mostly independent?" [shape=diamond];
31	    "Stay in this session?" [shape=diamond];
32	    "subagent-driven-development" [shape=box];
33	    "executing-plans" [shape=box];
34	    "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [shape=box];
35	
36	    "Have implementation plan?" -> "Tasks mostly independent?" [label="yes"];
37	    "Have implementation plan?" -> "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [label="no"];
38	    "Tasks mostly independent?" -> "Stay in this session?" [label="yes"];
39	    "Tasks mostly independent?" -> "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [label="no - tightly coupled"];
40	    "Stay in this session?" -> "subagent-driven-development" [label="yes"];
41	    "Stay in this session?" -> "executing-plans" [label="no - parallel session"];
42	}
43	```
44	
45	**vs. Executing Plans (parallel session):**
46	- Same session (no context switch)
47	- Fresh subagent per task (no context pollution)
48	- Review after each task (spec compliance + code quality), broad review at the end
49	- Faster iteration (no human-in-loop between tasks)
50	
51	## The Process
52	
53	Each step's full text is in its own file beside this one. Read a step's file when you enter the step; after a compaction, the step table below names the one to read.
54	
55	1. **Setup** ([setup.md](setup.md)): sync the state branch and find the plan's workspace, settle where the work happens (hyperpowers:using-git-worktrees), create or read the ledger and append your session line, verify, read the plan and the spec, run the pre-flight scan. Setup's last action appends `session <sid>: setup complete`.
56	2. **Take a task and dispatch** ([task-loop.md](task-loop.md)): `scripts/sdd-state next` offers a task; claim the first and switch to its branch (none to take, or blocked: post, print the board, hand back). Dispatch the implementer, answer its questions, handle its report.
57	3. **Review the task** ([review-and-complete.md](review-and-complete.md)): generate the review package and dispatch the task reviewer. Blocking findings go to step 4; a finding that conflicts with the plan text goes to your human partner first.
58	4. **Fix loop** ([fix-loop.md](fix-loop.md)): fix rounds, each with a scoped re-review, under the shared cap in the rules below. When no finding is left open, go back to review-and-complete.md for the gate.
59	5. **Codex task gate and completion** ([review-and-complete.md](review-and-complete.md)): unless the task's effective tier is low, run the per-task Codex gate (blocking findings re-enter step 4). Append the `approved` line, merge back, detach, delete the task branch, and run `scripts/sdd-state complete`; any status but `complete` stops. Then step 2.
60	6. **Final review and Finish** ([final-and-finish.md](final-and-finish.md)): when no task remains, claim the final train, dispatch the final reviewer (one fix dispatch, one scoped re-review), the decision extractor and the Codex final gate, delete the workspace, then use hyperpowers:finishing-a-development-branch.
61	
62	## After a compaction: the step table
63	
64	Print the board (`scripts/sdd-state board PLAN_FILE`) and the ledger lines of your task and your Setup (`grep -E '^(Task <N>:|session <sid>: setup complete)' <workspace>/progress.md`, leaving out `Task <N>:` when you hold no task); `scripts/sdd-dir PLAN_FILE` prints the workspace. Do not Read the whole ledger after a compaction: it grows with the plan. A row's newest line is the newest of your task's lines the table names (its branch, base, implementer identity, `report`, `review`, Codex gate round, `approved`, `merged` and `fix round` lines); a line it does not name, such as a deferred minor or the gate directory, leaves your step unchanged. Then Read the step file this table names:
65	
66	| State | Step file |
67	|---|---|
68	| no ledger in the workspace, or no `setup complete` line of this session in it | [setup.md](setup.md) |
69	| the board shows no task held by this session and a task without a completion line | [task-loop.md](task-loop.md) |
70	| the held task's newest line is its branch, base, implementer identity or `report` line | [task-loop.md](task-loop.md) |
71	| its newest line is a `review` or Codex gate line approving it, an `approved` line or a `merged` line | [review-and-complete.md](review-and-complete.md) |
72	| its newest line is a `fix round` line, or a `review` or Codex gate line with blocking findings | [fix-loop.md](fix-loop.md) |
73	| this session holds the final claim, or every task has a completion line | [final-and-finish.md](final-and-finish.md) |
74	
75	A state the table does not cover reads [task-loop.md](task-loop.md), and you record that in the ledger.
76	
77	The table reads these ledger lines, so write each one where its step says:
78	
79	- `session <sid>: setup complete`, Setup's last action;
80	- `Task <N>: report <status> <one line>`, after an implementer's report;
81	- `Task <N>: review <approved|blocking> <reviewer id> <one line>`, after a task review or scoped re-review;
82	- `Task <N>: codex gate round <R> <approved|blocking> <one line>`, after each per-task Codex gate round.
83	
84	## Rules for every step
85	
86	These hold in every step file. Where a step file and this section differ, this section governs.
87	
88	- Tasks with a `Task <N>: complete` line are DONE — do not re-dispatch them. Conversation memory does not survive compaction. After compaction, trust the ledger and `git log` over your own recollection.
89	- Dispatch implementer, task-reviewer, fix-round, re-review and final-reviewer subagents with `run_in_background: false`. Your next step always depends on the result, and a foreground call keeps your turn open, which is what an editor such as Zed shows as the session working. A background dispatch ends the turn while the subagent runs, and the editor shows the session idle.
90	- Run a covering command expected to finish within 10 minutes in the foreground, with an explicit timeout of at least its expected runtime and at most 600000 ms. A command that may run past 10 minutes is a tracked job; [task-loop.md](task-loop.md), "Waiting on subagents and long commands", gives its commands and watch budget.
91	- One implementer at a time in this session: parallel work is other sessions' (one controller per task branch); never dispatch two implementers at once here.
92	- Never fix findings yourself in the controller session — your context stays clean for coordination, and controller fixes skip review. The one exception is the de-minimis fix in [fix-loop.md](fix-loop.md).
93	- The task reviewer's blocking findings and the per-task Codex gate's blocking findings form one loop with ONE shared cap of **five rounds per task**: the gate does not run a count of its own.
94	- When round 5's re-review — or a per-task Codex gate at the spent cap — still leaves blocking findings open, stop dispatching and surface the task as BLOCKED, as [fix-loop.md](fix-loop.md) describes under the breaker.
95	
96	## Model Selection
97	
98	Match the model to the task's difficulty rather than defaulting. Two rules are
99	defaults you will get wrong by omission, so they stay here: **always specify
100	the model explicitly when dispatching a subagent** — an omitted model inherits
101	your session's, usually the most capable and most expensive — and **a mid-tier
102	model is the floor for reviewers and for implementers working from prose
103	descriptions**, whatever the schedule pressure. The cheapest tier is for
104	transcription, where the task's own text carries the complete code to write,
105	and for single-file mechanical fixes. The per-role guidance, the complexity
106	signals, and the fix-loop escalation rule are in
107	[model-selection.md](model-selection.md).
108	
109	## The waiting board
110	
111	Before you ask your human partner a question, hand back BLOCKED, meet an
112	empty frontier (`held` or `blocked`), or stop on a merge conflict, post what
113	you wait on: `scripts/sdd-state wait PLAN_FILE --session <sid> --kind
114	<question|tasks|merge|gate|handoff> [--task N] --note "<one line>"`, and put
115	the session lines of `scripts/sdd-state board PLAN_FILE` in what you write.
116	When you resume, clear it: `scripts/sdd-state wait PLAN_FILE --session <sid> --clear`.
117	The board is how your human partner finds the session that needs them among
118	several; a session that holds a claim and posts nothing shows as quiet

results.content:
### 4. The fix loop

Part of [SKILL.md](SKILL.md); the rules there hold in this step.

The loop triggers when the review reports spec ❌, any Critical or Important
finding, a ⚠️ item you confirmed as a real gap, or a blocking finding from
the per-task Codex gate in [review-and-complete.md](review-and-complete.md).

Task-reviewer findings are claims too. The fixing implementer verifies
each finding against the code before fixing it
(hyperpowers:receiving-code-review); a finding is declined only as
refuted or corrected with file:line evidence, which the controller
records in the ledger; a confirmed finding is fixed or carried open; a
finding nobody can settle stays open and counts against the round cap.

Before the loop starts, two routes leave it immediately:

- Record Minor findings in the progress ledger as you go
  (`Task <N>: minor (deferred): <one-liner>`), and point the final
  whole-branch review at that list so it can triage which must be fixed
  before merge. A roll-up nobody reads is a silent discard. Minor findings
  never enter the loop.
- A finding labeled plan-mandated — or any finding that conflicts with what
  the plan's text requires — is your human partner's decision: present the
  finding and the plan text beside it and ask which governs. Do not dismiss
  the finding because the plan mandates it, and do not dispatch a fix that
  contradicts the plan without asking.

Everything else enters the loop — the Claude task reviewer's blocking
findings and the per-task Codex gate's blocking findings alike. They share
the five-round cap SKILL.md sets. A fix round is one fix dispatch — or one
controller-applied de-minimis fix — plus one scoped re-review.

**Rounds 1-3 — the same model, carrying the task's record.** Where the Agent
tool offers `run_in_background` (Claude Code outside fork mode), dispatch a
fresh implementer in the foreground (`run_in_background: false`) with the
brief path, the report-file path, and the open findings verbatim, on the
original implementer's model (the `model` in its ledger identity line);
tell it a prior implementer did the
task and the report file records what it did and tried. A foreground
dispatch keeps your turn open until the fix returns, so a fix round on
Claude Code dispatches a fresh foreground implementer; a SendMessage resume
is for harnesses without the option, Claude Code's fork mode among them. On
those harnesses, resume the original
implementer with the findings verbatim: its context is intact. If the
harness cannot message a live subagent either, dispatch a fresh implementer
with the brief path, the report-file path, and the findings; the report file
is the persistent memory either way.

**Rounds 4-5 — dispatch a fresh takeover implementer on a more capable
model** (per Model Selection in SKILL.md), with the brief path, the report-file path,
the open findings, and this framing: "A prior implementer attempted this
task [N] times; you own it now. Read the report file for what was tried." A
loop that survives three rounds usually means the same model cannot see
its own problem: the takeover brings a more capable one.

**Every round, either way:** the implementer fixes, re-runs the tests
covering the amended code, appends its fix report to the same report file,
and returns the short contract. Before re-dispatching the reviewer, confirm
the fix report contains the covering tests, the command run, and the
output; dispatch the re-review once all three are present. That
precondition covers the findings the round fixed; a round that declines
every finding is defined below. Name the covering test files in the fix
message — a one-line fix does not need the whole suite. The per-task loop
gives a fix round to an implementer rather than a fixer, so it never uses
[fix-subagent-prompt.md](fix-subagent-prompt.md) — that template belongs to
the final review's one fix wave.

**The re-review is scoped.** Run `scripts/review-package PLAN_FILE FIX_BASE HEAD`
where FIX_BASE is the head the previous review saw, and dispatch
[re-review-prompt.md](re-review-prompt.md) with the findings list, the
brief, the report file, and the printed diff path. The re-reviewer verdicts
each finding ADDRESSED, NOT ADDRESSED, or DECLINED — a refuted or corrected
finding whose file:line evidence the re-reviewer has confirmed; an unconfirmed
decline stays NOT ADDRESSED — and flags new breakage in the fix diff only. The
controller records each DECLINED finding in the ledger with its evidence. New
Critical/Important breakage in the fix diff joins the open findings list.
Out-of-scope observations go to the ledger as deferred minors — they never
extend the loop. Every round in this loop ends with the scoped re-review —
never a full task-reviewer re-run, whatever the finding's origin. Append the `Task <N>: review ...`
line (SKILL.md's ledger lines) after the round's `fix round` line, so the
newest line tells a resumed session whether the round left findings open.

**A round that declines every finding changes no code.** There is no fix
diff and no covering test to confirm; the implementer's report is the
artifact, carrying for each finding the refuted or corrected evidence at
file:line. Skip `scripts/review-package` for that round — its range is
empty — and dispatch the scoped re-review with the findings list, the brief,
the report, and the previous review's package path, so the re-reviewer
verdicts each finding DECLINED or NOT ADDRESSED from the evidence alone. The
covering-tests precondition applies only to findings that were fixed. Record
the round as `(0 addressed, <Y> declined, <Z> open)`; a NOT ADDRESSED verdict
keeps that finding open and the round counts toward the cap as usual.

**After each round,** append to the ledger:
`Task <N>: fix round <R>/5 (<X> addressed, <Y> declined, <Z> open — <finding one-liners>; commits <a7>..<b7>)`

One narrow exception to the controller rule in SKILL.md: a fix fully specified by the finding itself — exact file, exact
lines, exact replacement, no judgment left — touching at most 3 lines in
one file with no new logic, may be controller-applied — one finding per
reach; a round holding two such findings is not de minimis. The exception
waives nothing else: it consumes a fix round and ends in the same scoped
re-review; the controller applies the edit and runs the fix's covering
command FIRST — a failure means the fix was not de minimis: revert the
edit, spend no round, and go back to the round's own rule — then commits
the verified fix (the re-review packages committed diffs — an
uncommitted fix hands it nothing) and appends the fix report — the
command, its output, and a diff summary — to the task's report file
itself, exactly as an implementer would. Its ledger line keeps the
fix-round schema with the marker inside it:
`Task <N>: fix round <R>/5 controller-applied (de minimis) (<X> addressed, <Y> declined, <Z> open — <finding one-liners>; commits <a7>..<b7>)`.
Reaching for it twice in the same task means the findings are not de
minimis — go back to the round's own rule: hand the findings to an
implementer at rounds 1-3, dispatch the takeover at rounds 4-5.

When the re-review leaves no finding open, go to the per-task Codex gate in [review-and-complete.md](review-and-complete.md), or, for an effective-low task, to step 5 there.

**The breaker.** At the spent cap SKILL.md stops dispatching. The task
does not silently continue and nothing is parked on your own authority:
surface the open findings to your human partner as BLOCKED, each with the
rounds already spent, what was tried, and the evidence. Ledger it:
`Task <N>: BLOCKED at cap — <finding one-liners>`. They decide what happens
next.

5	
6	# Subagent-Driven Development
7	
8	Execute plan by dispatching a fresh implementer subagent per task, a task review (spec compliance + code quality) after each, and a broad whole-branch review at the end.
9	
10	**Why subagents:** You delegate tasks to specialized agents with isolated context. By precisely crafting their instructions and context, you ensure they stay focused and succeed at their task. They should never inherit your session's context or history — you construct exactly what they need. This also preserves your own context for coordination work.
11	
12	**Core principle:** Fresh subagent per task + task review (spec + quality) + broad final review = high quality, fast iteration
13	
14	**Narration:** between tool calls, narrate at most one short line — the
15	ledger and the tool results carry the record.
16	
17	**REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use hyperpowers:communication for anything you write to your human partner in this skill: the pre-flight question, an escalation, a BLOCKED hand-back.
18	
19	**Continuous execution:** Do not pause to check in with your human partner between tasks. Execute all tasks from the plan without stopping. While the plan has tasks left, a turn ends in exactly three cases: a BLOCKED status you cannot resolve; a question only your human partner can answer, asked in that message (ambiguity that genuinely prevents progress is such a question); or, on a harness that cannot wait in the foreground, tracked work still running, named in that message. A message that names your next step is followed by that step's tool call in the same turn. "Tasks 1 and 2 are done. Moving to Task 3." followed by a turn end is a stop: your human partner reads it as work in progress, and nothing resumes it until they type. Completing the last task does not end the plan: it opens the final whole-branch review, and the plan ends only after Finish. Each permitted turn end, and "your human partner asked you to stop", is written to the ledger in the same message that ends the turn: run `scripts/sdd-state handback PLAN_FILE --reason "<why>"` (add `--session <sid>` on a harness without `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`; `busy` or `error` is retried, and without the line the guard falls back to reading your last message). Write that line only for a question only your human partner can answer, a BLOCKED report, or their request to stop; finishing the tasks is never a reason for it. On Claude Code the SDD stop guard refuses a turn end it can prove is premature, two consecutive attempts per plan, the count resetting after any allow, with this message: "SDD stop guard: plan <plan path> is not finished (<state>; nothing tracked is live). Take the next step now, in this turn. If you are handing back to your human partner (a question only they can answer, a BLOCKED report, or they asked you to stop), run scripts/sdd-state handback PLAN_FILE --session <sid> --reason "<why>" and end the turn with that message." (with a live job the first sentences name the job and say to watch it with `tracked-job wait`). When you meet it, take the next step; writing a question you do not need answered to get past it is the stop it exists to prevent, and the log records every allow. "Should I continue?" prompts and progress summaries waste their time — they asked you to execute the plan, so execute it.

The harness never reports on such a process, so nothing wakes you when it ends, and a turn you end to wait for it does not resume.

23	**After every context compaction:** this file fits within the 20,000 characters Claude Code re-attaches, so the copy you hold is whole. 1	### 4. The fix loop
2	
3	Part of [SKILL.md](SKILL.md); the rules there hold in this step.
4	
5	The loop triggers when the review reports spec ❌, any Critical or Important
6	finding, a ⚠️ item you confirmed as a real gap, or a blocking finding from
7	the per-task Codex gate in [review-and-complete.md](review-and-complete.md).
8	
9	Task-reviewer findings are claims too. The fixing implementer verifies
10	each finding against the code before fixing it
11	(hyperpowers:receiving-code-review); a finding is declined only as
12	refuted or corrected with file:line evidence, which the controller
13	records in the ledger; a confirmed finding is fixed or carried open; a
14	finding nobody can settle stays open and counts against the round cap.
15	
16	Before the loop starts, two routes leave it immediately:
17	
18	- Record Minor findings in the progress ledger as you go
19	  (`Task <N>: minor (deferred): <one-liner>`), and point the final
20	  whole-branch review at that list so it can triage which must be fixed
21	  before merge. A roll-up nobody reads is a silent discard. Minor findings
22	  never enter the loop.
23	- A finding labeled plan-mandated — or any finding that conflicts with what
24	  the plan's text requires — is your human partner's decision: present the
25	  finding and the plan text beside it and ask which governs. Do not dismiss
26	  the finding because the plan mandates it, and do not dispatch a fix that
27	  contradicts the plan without asking.
28	
29	Everything else enters the loop — the Claude task reviewer's blocking
30	findings and the per-task Codex gate's blocking findings alike. They share
31	the five-round cap SKILL.md sets. A fix round is one fix dispatch — or one
32	controller-applied de-minimis fix — plus one scoped re-review.
33	
34	**Rounds 1-3 — the same model, carrying the task's record.** Where the Agent
35	tool offers `run_in_background` (Claude Code outside fork mode), dispatch a
36	fresh implementer in the foreground (`run_in_background: false`) with the
37	brief path, the report-file path, and the open findings verbatim, on the
38	original implementer's model (the `model` in its ledger identity line);
39	tell it a prior implementer did the
40	task and the report file records what it did and tried. A foreground
41	dispatch keeps your turn open until the fix returns, so a fix round on
42	Claude Code dispatches a fresh foreground implementer; a SendMessage resume
43	is for harnesses without the option, Claude Code's fork mode among them. On
44	those harnesses, resume the original
45	implementer with the findings verbatim: its context is intact. If the
46	harness cannot message a live subagent either, dispatch a fresh implementer
47	with the brief path, the report-file path, and the findings; the report file
48	is the persistent memory either way.
49	
50	**Rounds 4-5 — dispatch a fresh takeover implementer on a more capable
51	model** (per Model Selection in SKILL.md), with the brief path, the report-file path,
52	the open findings, and this framing: "A prior implementer attempted this
53	task [N] times; you own it now. Read the report file for what was tried." A
54	loop that survives three rounds usually means the same model cannot see
55	its own problem: the takeover brings a more capable one.
56	
57	**Every round, either way:** the implementer fixes, re-runs the tests
58	covering the amended code, appends its fix report to the same report file,
59	and returns the short contract. Before re-dispatching the reviewer, confirm
60	the fix report contains the covering tests, the command run, and the
61	output; dispatch the re-review once all three are present. That
62	precondition covers the findings the round fixed; a round that declines
63	every finding is defined below. Name the covering test files in the fix
64	message — a one-line fix does not need the whole suite. The per-task loop
65	gives a fix round to an implementer rather than a fixer, so it never uses
66	[fix-subagent-prompt.md](fix-subagent-prompt.md) — that template belongs to
67	the final review's one fix wave.
68	
69	**The re-review is scoped.** Run `scripts/review-package PLAN_FILE FIX_BASE HEAD`
70	where FIX_BASE is the head the previous review saw, and dispatch
71	[re-review-prompt.md](re-review-prompt.md) with the findings list, the
72	brief, the report file, and the printed diff path. The re-reviewer verdicts
73	each finding ADDRESSED, NOT ADDRESSED, or DECLINED — a refuted or corrected
74	finding whose file:line evidence the re-reviewer has confirmed; an unconfirmed
75	decline stays NOT ADDRESSED — and flags new breakage in the fix diff only. The
76	controller records each DECLINED finding in the ledger with its evidence. New
77	Critical/Important breakage in the fix diff joins the open findings list.
78	Out-of-scope observations go to the ledger as deferred minors — they never
79	extend the loop. Every round in this loop ends with the scoped re-review —
80	never a full task-reviewer re-run, whatever the finding's origin. Append the `Task <N>: review ...`
81	line (SKILL.md's ledger lines) after the round's `fix round` line, so the
82	newest line tells a resumed session whether the round left findings open.
83	
84	**A round that declines every finding changes no code.** There is no fix
85	diff and no covering test to confirm; the implementer's report is the
86	artifact, carrying for each finding the refuted or corrected evidence at
87	file:line. Skip `scripts/review-package` for that round — its range is
88	empty — and dispatch the scoped re-review with the findings list, the brief,
89	the report, and the previous review's package path, so the re-reviewer
90	verdicts each finding DECLINED or NOT ADDRESSED from the evidence alone. The
91	covering-tests precondition applies only to findings that were fixed. Record
92	the round as `(0 addressed, <Y> declined, <Z> open)`; a NOT ADDRESSED verdict
93	keeps that finding open and the round counts toward the cap as usual.
94	
95	**After each round,** append to the ledger:
96	`Task <N>: fix round <R>/5 (<X> addressed, <Y> declined, <Z> open — <finding one-liners>; commits <a7>..<b7>)`
97	
98	One narrow exception to the controller rule in SKILL.md: a fix fully specified by the finding itself — exact file, exact
99	lines, exact replacement, no judgment left — touching at most 3 lines in
100	one file with no new logic, may be controller-applied — one finding per
101	reach; a round holding two such findings is not de minimis. The exception
102	waives nothing else: it consumes a fix round and ends in the same scoped
103	re-review; the controller applies the edit and runs the fix's covering
104	command FIRST — a failure means the fix was not de minimis: revert the
105	edit, spend no round, and go back to the round's own rule — then commits
106	the verified fix (the re-review packages committed diffs — an
107	uncommitted fix hands it nothing) and appends the fix report — the
108	command, its output, and a diff summary — to the task's report file
109	itself, exactly as an implementer would. Its ledger line keeps the
110	fix-round schema with the marker inside it:
111	`Task <N>: fix round <R>/5 controller-applied (de minimis) (<X> addressed, <Y> declined, <Z> open — <finding one-liners>; commits <a7>..<b7>)`.
112	Reaching for it twice in the same task means the findings are not de
113	minimis — go back to the round's own rule: hand the findings to an
114	implementer at rounds 1-3, dispatch the takeover at rounds 4-5.
115	
116	When the re-review leaves no finding open, go to the per-task Codex gate in [review-and-complete.md](review-and-complete.md), or, for an effective-low task, to step 5 there.
117	
118	**The breaker.** At the spent cap SKILL.md stops dispatching. The task
119	does not silently continue and nothing is parked on your own authority:
120	surface the open findings to your human partner as BLOCKED, each with the
121	rounds already spent, what was tried, and the evidence. Ledger it:
122	`Task <N>: BLOCKED at cap — <finding one-liners>`. They decide what happens
123	next.

6	# Subagent-Driven Development
7	
8	Execute plan by dispatching a fresh implementer subagent per task, a task review (spec compliance + code quality) after each, and a broad whole-branch review at the end.
9	
10	**Why subagents:** You delegate tasks to specialized agents with isolated context. By precisely crafting their instructions and context, you ensure they stay focused and succeed at their task. They should never inherit your session's context or history — you construct exactly what they need. This also preserves your own context for coordination work.
11	
12	**Core principle:** Fresh subagent per task + task review (spec + quality) + broad final review = high quality, fast iteration
13	
14	**Narration:** between tool calls, narrate at most one short line — the
15	ledger and the tool results carry the record.
16	
17	**REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use hyperpowers:communication for anything you write to your human partner in this skill: the pre-flight question, an escalation, a BLOCKED hand-back.
18	
19	**Continuous execution:** Do not pause to check in with your human partner between tasks. Execute all tasks from the plan without stopping. While the plan has tasks left, a turn ends in exactly three cases: a BLOCKED status you cannot resolve; a question only your human partner can answer, asked in that message (ambiguity that genuinely prevents progress is such a question); or, on a harness that cannot wait in the foreground, tracked work still running, named in that message. A message that names your next step is followed by that step's tool call in the same turn. "Tasks 1 and 2 are done. Moving to Task 3." followed by a turn end is a stop: your human partner reads it as work in progress, and nothing resumes it until they type. Completing the last task does not end the plan: it opens the final whole-branch review, and the plan ends only after Finish. Each permitted turn end, and "your human partner asked you to stop", is written to the ledger in the same message that ends the turn: run `scripts/sdd-state handback PLAN_FILE --reason "<why>"` (add `--session <sid>` on a harness without `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`; `busy` or `error` is retried, and without the line the guard falls back to reading your last message). Write that line only for a question only your human partner can answer, a BLOCKED report, or their request to stop; finishing the tasks is never a reason for it. On Claude Code the SDD stop guard refuses a turn end it can prove is premature, two consecutive attempts per plan, the count resetting after any allow, with this message: "SDD stop guard: plan <plan path> is not finished (<state>; nothing tracked is live). Take the next step now, in this turn. If you are handing back to your human partner (a question only they can answer, a BLOCKED report, or they asked you to stop), run scripts/sdd-state handback PLAN_FILE --session <sid> --reason "<why>" and end the turn with that message." (with a live job the first sentences name the job and say to watch it with `tracked-job wait`). When you meet it, take the next step; writing a question you do not need answered to get past it is the stop it exists to prevent, and the log records every allow. "Should I continue?" prompts and progress summaries waste their time — they asked you to execute the plan, so execute it.
20	
21	**Tracked work only:** anything that outlives one tool call starts through your harness's tracked background option (`run_in_background` on Claude Code); never start it with a trailing `&`, `nohup`, `setsid`, `disown`, or a script that detaches a process. The harness never reports on such a process, so nothing wakes you when it ends, and a turn you end to wait for it does not resume.
22	
23	**After every context compaction:** this file fits within the 20,000 characters Claude Code re-attaches, so the copy you hold is whole. A step file you read before the compaction does not survive it. Before your next action, print the board and the ledger lines the step table names (your task's and your Setup's, never the whole ledger), find your step in the table, and Read that step file in full.
24	
25	## When to Use
26	
27	```dot
28	digraph when_to_use {
29	    "Have implementation plan?" [shape=diamond];
30	    "Tasks mostly independent?" [shape=diamond];
31	    "Stay in this session?" [shape=diamond];
32	    "subagent-driven-development" [shape=box];
33	    "executing-plans" [shape=box];
34	    "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [shape=box];
35	
36	    "Have implementation plan?" -> "Tasks mostly independent?" [label="yes"];
37	    "Have implementation plan?" -> "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [label="no"];
38	    "Tasks mostly independent?" -> "Stay in this session?" [label="yes"];
39	    "Tasks mostly independent?" -> "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [label="no - tightly coupled"];
40	    "Stay in this session?" -> "subagent-driven-development" [label="yes"];
41	    "Stay in this session?" -> "executing-plans" [label="no - parallel session"];
42	}
43	```
44	
45	**vs. Executing Plans (parallel session):**
46	- Same session (no context switch)
47	- Fresh subagent per task (no context pollution)
48	- Review after each task (spec compliance + code quality), broad review at the end
49	- Faster iteration (no human-in-loop between tasks)
50	
51	## The Process
52	
53	Each step's full text is in its own file beside this one. Read a step's file when you enter the step; after a compaction, the step table below names the one to read.
54	
55	1. **Setup** ([setup.md](setup.md)): sync the state branch and find the plan's workspace, settle where the work happens (hyperpowers:using-git-worktrees), create or read the ledger and append your session line, verify, read the plan and the spec, run the pre-flight scan. Setup's last action appends `session <sid>: setup complete`.
56	2. **Take a task and dispatch** ([task-loop.md](task-loop.md)): `scripts/sdd-state next` offers a task; claim the first and switch to its branch (none to take, or blocked: post, print the board, hand back). Dispatch the implementer, answer its questions, handle its report.
57	3. **Review the task** ([review-and-complete.md](review-and-complete.md)): generate the review package and dispatch the task reviewer. Blocking findings go to step 4; a finding that conflicts with the plan text goes to your human partner first.
58	4. **Fix loop** ([fix-loop.md](fix-loop.md)): fix rounds, each with a scoped re-review, under the shared cap in the rules below. When no finding is left open, go back to review-and-complete.md for the gate.
59	5. **Codex task gate and completion** ([review-and-complete.md](review-and-complete.md)): unless the task's effective tier is low, run the per-task Codex gate (blocking findings re-enter step 4). Append the `approved` line, merge back, detach, delete the task branch, and run `scripts/sdd-state complete`; any status but `complete` stops. Then step 2.
60	6. **Final review and Finish** ([final-and-finish.md](final-and-finish.md)): when no task remains, claim the final train, dispatch the final reviewer (one fix dispatch, one scoped re-review), the decision extractor and the Codex final gate, delete the workspace, then use hyperpowers:finishing-a-development-branch.
61	
62	## After a compaction: the step table
63	
64	Print the board (`scripts/sdd-state board PLAN_FILE`) and the ledger lines of your task and your Setup (`grep -E '^(Task <N>:|session <sid>: setup complete)' <workspace>/progress.md`, leaving out `Task <N>:` when you hold no task); `scripts/sdd-dir PLAN_FILE` prints the workspace. Do not Read the whole ledger after a compaction: it grows with the plan. A row's newest line is the newest of your task's lines the table names (its branch, base, implementer identity, `report`, `review`, Codex gate round, `approved`, `merged` and `fix round` lines); a line it does not name, such as a deferred minor or the gate directory, leaves your step unchanged. Then Read the step file this table names:
65	
66	| State | Step file |
67	|---|---|
68	| no ledger in the workspace, or no `setup complete` line of this session in it | [setup.md](setup.md) |
69	| the board shows no task held by this session and a task without a completion line | [task-loop.md](task-loop.md) |
70	| the held task's newest line is its branch, base, implementer identity or `report` line | [task-loop.md](task-loop.md) |
71	| its newest line is a `review` or Codex gate line approving it, an `approved` line or a `merged` line | [review-and-complete.md](review-and-complete.md) |
72	| its newest line is a `fix round` line, or a `review` or Codex gate line with blocking findings | [fix-loop.md](fix-loop.md) |
73	| this session holds the final claim, or every task has a completion line | [final-and-finish.md](final-and-finish.md) |
74	
75	A state the table does not cover reads [task-loop.md](task-loop.md), and you record that in the ledger.
76	
77	The table reads these ledger lines, so write each one where its step says:
78	
79	- `session <sid>: setup complete`, Setup's last action;
80	- `Task <N>: report <status> <one line>`, after an implementer's report;
81	- `Task <N>: review <approved|blocking> <reviewer id> <one line>`, after a task review or scoped re-review;
82	- `Task <N>: codex gate round <R> <approved|blocking> <one line>`, after each per-task Codex gate round.
83	
84	## Rules for every step
85	
86	These hold in every step file. Where a step file and this section differ, this section governs.
87	
88	- Tasks with a `Task <N>: complete` line are DONE — do not re-dispatch them. Conversation memory does not survive compaction. After compaction, trust the ledger and `git log` over your own recollection.
89	- Dispatch implementer, task-reviewer, fix-round, re-review and final-reviewer subagents with `run_in_background: false`. Your next step always depends on the result, and a foreground call keeps your turn open, which is what an editor such as Zed shows as the session working. A background dispatch ends the turn while the subagent runs, and the editor shows the session idle.
90	- Run a covering command expected to finish within 10 minutes in the foreground, with an explicit timeout of at least its expected runtime and at most 600000 ms. A command that may run past 10 minutes is a tracked job; [task-loop.md](task-loop.md), "Waiting on subagents and long commands", gives its commands and watch budget.
91	- One implementer at a time in this session: parallel work is other sessions' (one controller per task branch); never dispatch two implementers at once here.
92	- Never fix findings yourself in the controller session — your context stays clean for coordination, and controller fixes skip review. The one exception is the de-minimis fix in [fix-loop.md](fix-loop.md).
93	- The task reviewer's blocking findings and the per-task Codex gate's blocking findings form one loop with ONE shared cap of **five rounds per task**: the gate does not run a count of its own.
94	- When round 5's re-review — or a per-task Codex gate at the spent cap — still leaves blocking findings open, stop dispatching and surface the task as BLOCKED, as [fix-loop.md](fix-loop.md) describes under the breaker.
95	
96	## Model Selection
97	
98	Match the model to the task's difficulty rather than defaulting. Two rules are
99	defaults you will get wrong by omission, so they stay here: **always specify
100	the model explicitly when dispatching a subagent** — an omitted model inherits
101	your session's, usually the most capable and most expensive — and **a mid-tier
102	model is the floor for reviewers and for implementers working from prose
103	descriptions**, whatever the schedule pressure. The cheapest tier is for
104	transcription, where the task's own text carries the complete code to write,
105	and for single-file mechanical fixes. The per-role guidance, the complexity
106	signals, and the fix-loop escalation rule are in
107	[model-selection.md](model-selection.md).
108	
109	## The waiting board
110	
111	Before you ask your human partner a question, hand back BLOCKED, meet an
112	empty frontier (`held` or `blocked`), or stop on a merge conflict, post what
113	you wait on: `scripts/sdd-state wait PLAN_FILE --session <sid> --kind
114	<question|tasks|merge|gate|handoff> [--task N] --note "<one line>"`, and put
115	the session lines of `scripts/sdd-state board PLAN_FILE` in what you write.
116	When you resume, clear it: `scripts/sdd-state wait PLAN_FILE --session <sid> --clear`.
117	The board is how your human partner finds the session that needs them among
118	several; a session that holds a claim and posts nothing shows as quiet
119	after half an hour, which is where they look for a permission prompt.
120	
121	## Risk Tiers (per-task Codex gate applicability)
122	
123	Tiers are `low`, `standard`, `high`, declared per task in the plan. A task
124	skips the per-task Codex gate only when all three hold: declared low, the
125	plan's own Codex gate actually reviewed the plan, and no escalation trigger
126	fired at any point during execution. That skip is recorded durably. An
127	unreviewed low tier — plan gate skipped, degraded, or outcome unknown —
128	executes as standard, and a task demoted that way runs the full train and
129	records NO tier-skip event. The Claude task reviewer and the final
130	whole-branch train never tier off. When any task did skip, write
131	`tier-skips.md` in this plan's workspace; Final Review hands its path to the
132	final reviewer and the final Codex gate. The escalation triggers, the
133	fallback rules, and the exact ledger line shape are in
134	[risk-tiers.md](risk-tiers.md) — read it before dispatching any task declared
135	low.
136	
137	## Common Rationalizations
138	
139	The excuses that show up mid-run and what is actually true:
140	[common-rationalizations.md](common-rationalizations.md). Read it the moment you
141	catch yourself justifying a shortcut.
142	
143	## Example Workflow
144	
145	A complete worked run, dispatch through finish:
146	[example-workflow.md](example-workflow.md).

1	### 4. The fix loop
2	
3	Part of [SKILL.md](SKILL.md); the rules there hold in this step.
4	
5	The loop triggers when the review reports spec ❌, any Critical or Important
6	finding, a ⚠️ item you confirmed as a real gap, or a blocking finding from
7	the per-task Codex gate in [review-and-complete.md](review-and-complete.md).
8	
9	Task-reviewer findings are claims too. The fixing implementer verifies
10	each finding against the code before fixing it
11	(hyperpowers:receiving-code-review); a finding is declined only as
12	refuted or corrected with file:line evidence, which the controller
13	records in the ledger; a confirmed finding is fixed or carried open; a
14	finding nobody can settle stays open and counts against the round cap.
15	
16	Before the loop starts, two routes leave it immediately:
17	
18	- Record Minor findings in the progress ledger as you go
19	  (`Task <N>: minor (deferred): <one-liner>`), and point the final
20	  whole-branch review at that list so it can triage which must be fixed
21	  before merge. A roll-up nobody reads is a silent discard. Minor findings
22	  never enter the loop.
23	- A finding labeled plan-mandated — or any finding that conflicts with what
24	  the plan's text requires — is your human partner's decision: present the
25	  finding and the plan text beside it and ask which governs. Do not dismiss
26	  the finding because the plan mandates it, and do not dispatch a fix that
27	  contradicts the plan without asking.
28	
29	Everything else enters the loop — the Claude task reviewer's blocking
30	findings and the per-task Codex gate's blocking findings alike. They share
31	the five-round cap SKILL.md sets. A fix round is one fix dispatch — or one
32	controller-applied de-minimis fix — plus one scoped re-review.
33	
34	**Rounds 1-3 — the same model, carrying the task's record.** Where the Agent
35	tool offers `run_in_background` (Claude Code outside fork mode), dispatch a
36	fresh implementer in the foreground (`run_in_background: false`) with the
37	brief path, the report-file path, and the open findings verbatim, on the
38	original implementer's model (the `model` in its ledger identity line);
39	tell it a prior implementer did the
40	task and the report file records what it did and tried. A foreground
41	dispatch keeps your turn open until the fix returns, so a fix round on
42	Claude Code dispatches a fresh foreground implementer; a SendMessage resume
43	is for harnesses without the option, Claude Code's fork mode among them. On
44	those harnesses, resume the original
45	implementer with the findings verbatim: its context is intact. If the
46	harness cannot message a live subagent either, dispatch a fresh implementer
47	with the brief path, the report-file path, and the findings; the report file
48	is the persistent memory either way.
49	
50	**Rounds 4-5 — dispatch a fresh takeover implementer on a more capable
51	model** (per Model Selection in SKILL.md), with the brief path, the report-file path,
52	the open findings, and this framing: "A prior implementer attempted this
53	task [N] times; you own it now. Read the report file for what was tried." A
54	loop that survives three rounds usually means the same model cannot see
55	its own problem: the takeover brings a more capable one.
56	
57	**Every round, either way:** the implementer fixes, re-runs the tests
58	covering the amended code, appends its fix report to the same report file,
59	and returns the short contract. Before re-dispatching the reviewer, confirm
60	the fix report contains the covering tests, the command run, and the
61	output; dispatch the re-review once all three are present. That
62	precondition covers the findings the round fixed; a round that declines
63	every finding is defined below. Name the covering test files in the fix
64	message — a one-line fix does not need the whole suite. The per-task loop
65	gives a fix round to an implementer rather than a fixer, so it never uses
66	[fix-subagent-prompt.md](fix-subagent-prompt.md) — that template belongs to
67	the final review's one fix wave.
68	
69	**The re-review is scoped.** Run `scripts/review-package PLAN_FILE FIX_BASE HEAD`
70	where FIX_BASE is the head the previous review saw, and dispatch
71	[re-review-prompt.md](re-review-prompt.md) with the findings list, the
72	brief, the report file, and the printed diff path. The re-reviewer verdicts
73	each finding ADDRESSED, NOT ADDRESSED, or DECLINED — a refuted or corrected
74	finding whose file:line evidence the re-reviewer has confirmed; an unconfirmed
75	decline stays NOT ADDRESSED — and flags new breakage in the fix diff only. The
76	controller records each DECLINED finding in the ledger with its evidence. New
77	Critical/Important breakage in the fix diff joins the open findings list.
78	Out-of-scope observations go to the ledger as deferred minors — they never
79	extend the loop. Every round in this loop ends with the scoped re-review —
80	never a full task-reviewer re-run, whatever the finding's origin. Append the `Task <N>: review ...`
81	line (SKILL.md's ledger lines) after the round's `fix round` line, so the
82	newest line tells a resumed session whether the round left findings open.
83	
84	**A round that declines every finding changes no code.** There is no fix
85	diff and no covering test to confirm; the implementer's report is the
86	artifact, carrying for each finding the refuted or corrected evidence at
87	file:line. Skip `scripts/review-package` for that round — its range is
88	empty — and dispatch the scoped re-review with the findings list, the brief,
89	the report, and the previous review's package path, so the re-reviewer
90	verdicts each finding DECLINED or NOT ADDRESSED from the evidence alone. The
91	covering-tests precondition applies only to findings that were fixed. Record
92	the round as `(0 addressed, <Y> declined, <Z> open)`; a NOT ADDRESSED verdict
93	keeps that finding open and the round counts toward the cap as usual.
94	
95	**After each round,** append to the ledger:
96	`Task <N>: fix round <R>/5 (<X> addressed, <Y> declined, <Z> open — <finding one-liners>; commits <a7>..<b7>)`
97	
98	One narrow exception to the controller rule in SKILL.md: a fix fully specified by the finding itself — exact file, exact
99	lines, exact replacement, no judgment left — touching at most 3 lines in
100	one file with no new logic, may be controller-applied — one finding per
101	reach; a round holding two such findings is not de minimis. The exception
102	waives nothing else: it consumes a fix round and ends in the same scoped
103	re-review; the controller applies the edit and runs the fix's covering
104	command FIRST — a failure means the fix was not de minimis: revert the
105	edit, spend no round, and go back to the round's own rule — then commits
106	the verified fix (the re-review packages committed diffs — an
107	uncommitted fix hands it nothing) and appends the fix report — the
108	command, its output, and a diff summary — to the task's report file
109	itself, exactly as an implementer would. Its ledger line keeps the
110	fix-round schema with the marker inside it:
111	`Task <N>: fix round <R>/5 controller-applied (de minimis) (<X> addressed, <Y> declined, <Z> open — <finding one-liners>; commits <a7>..<b7>)`.
112	Reaching for it twice in the same task means the findings are not de
113	minimis — go back to the round's own rule: hand the findings to an
114	implementer at rounds 1-3, dispatch the takeover at rounds 4-5.
115	
116	When the re-review leaves no finding open, go to the per-task Codex gate in [review-and-complete.md](review-and-complete.md), or, for an effective-low task, to step 5 there.
117	
118	**The breaker.** At the spent cap SKILL.md stops dispatching. The task
119	does not silently continue and nothing is parked on your own authority:
120	surface the open findings to your human partner as BLOCKED, each with the
121	rounds already spent, what was tried, and the evidence. Ledger it:
122	`Task <N>: BLOCKED at cap — <finding one-liners>`. They decide what happens
123	next.
124

# Scoped Re-Review Prompt Template

Use this template when dispatching a re-review after a fix round. The
re-reviewer verifies the findings were addressed or declined with
confirmed evidence and checks the fix diff for new breakage. It is not a
fresh review — the full review already happened.

**Purpose:** Verify each finding from the previous review was addressed or
declined with confirmed evidence, and that the fix itself broke nothing.

```
Subagent (general-purpose):
  description: "Re-review Task N fix round R"
  model: [MODEL — REQUIRED: choose per SKILL.md Model Selection; an omitted
         model silently inherits the session's most expensive one]
  run_in_background: false   # Claude Code: dispatch in the foreground (SKILL.md "Waiting on subagents"); omit on harnesses without the flag
  prompt: |
    You are re-reviewing one task's fix round. A previous review produced
    findings; an implementer has attempted to fix them. Your job is to
    verdict each finding and inspect the fix diff — nothing else.

    ## The Task

    Read the task brief: [BRIEF_FILE]

    ## The Findings Under Verification

    [FINDINGS]

    ## The Fix

    Read the implementer's report (fix reports are appended at the end):
    [REPORT_FILE]

    **Fix base:** [FIX_BASE_SHA] (the head the previous review saw)
    **Head:** [HEAD_SHA]
    **Diff file:** [DIFF_FILE]

    Read the diff file once — it contains the fix commits, a stat summary,
    and the fix diff with surrounding context. Do not re-run git commands.
    If the diff file is missing, fetch the diff yourself:
    `git diff --stat [FIX_BASE_SHA]..[HEAD_SHA]` and
    `git diff [FIX_BASE_SHA]..[HEAD_SHA]`.

    An all-declined round has no fix diff: the diff file above is then the
    previous review's package, and every finding's evidence lives in code that
    diff did not change. Read the cited file:line for each declined finding
    directly; nothing in this round is "outside the fix diff".

    Your review is read-only on this checkout. Do not mutate the working
    tree, the index, HEAD, or branch state in any way. Use tools like
    `git show`, `git diff`, and `git log` to inspect history. If you need a
    working copy of a different revision, check it out into a separate
    temporary directory (e.g. `git worktree add /tmp/review-[SHA] [SHA]`) —
    never move HEAD on this checkout.

    ## You Do Not Dispatch Subagents

    Do all of this review yourself. Never spawn a subagent to review part
    of the diff, and never spawn another reviewer for a second opinion.
    This process already provides every review seat the work gets; a
    reviewer you spawn duplicates one of them at full cost, and its

1	---
2	name: subagent-driven-development
3	description: Use when executing implementation plans with independent tasks in the current session
4	---
5	
6	# Subagent-Driven Development
7	
8	Execute plan by dispatching a fresh implementer subagent per task, a task review (spec compliance + code quality) after each, and a broad whole-branch review at the end.
9	
10	**Why subagents:** You delegate tasks to specialized agents with isolated context. By precisely crafting their instructions and context, you ensure they stay focused and succeed at their task. They should never inherit your session's context or history — you construct exactly what they need. This also preserves your own context for coordination work.
11	
12	**Core principle:** Fresh subagent per task + task review (spec + quality) + broad final review = high quality, fast iteration
13	
14	**Narration:** between tool calls, narrate at most one short line — the
15	ledger and the tool results carry the record.
16	
17	**REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use hyperpowers:communication for anything you write to your human partner in this skill: the pre-flight question, an escalation, a BLOCKED hand-back.
18	
19	**Continuous execution:** Do not pause to check in with your human partner between tasks. Execute all tasks from the plan without stopping. While the plan has tasks left, a turn ends in exactly three cases: a BLOCKED status you cannot resolve; a question only your human partner can answer, asked in that message (ambiguity that genuinely prevents progress is such a question); or, on a harness that cannot wait in the foreground, tracked work still running, named in that message. A message that names your next step is followed by that step's tool call in the same turn. "Tasks 1 and 2 are done. Moving to Task 3." followed by a turn end is a stop: your human partner reads it as work in progress, and nothing resumes it until they type. Completing the last task does not end the plan: it opens the final whole-branch review, and the plan ends only after Finish. Each permitted turn end, and "your human partner asked you to stop", is written to the ledger in the same message that ends the turn: run `scripts/sdd-state handback PLAN_FILE --reason "<why>"` (add `--session <sid>` on a harness without `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`; `busy` or `error` is retried, and without the line the guard falls back to reading your last message). Write that line only for a question only your human partner can answer, a BLOCKED report, or their request to stop; finishing the tasks is never a reason for it. On Claude Code the SDD stop guard refuses a turn end it can prove is premature, two consecutive attempts per plan, the count resetting after any allow, with this message: "SDD stop guard: plan <plan path> is not finished (<state>; nothing tracked is live). Take the next step now, in this turn. If you are handing back to your human partner (a question only they can answer, a BLOCKED report, or they asked you to stop), run scripts/sdd-state handback PLAN_FILE --session <sid> --reason "<why>" and end the turn with that message." (with a live job the first sentences name the job and say to watch it with `tracked-job wait`). When you meet it, take the next step; writing a question you do not need answered to get past it is the stop it exists to prevent, and the log records every allow. "Should I continue?" prompts and progress summaries waste their time — they asked you to execute the plan, so execute it.
20	
21	**Tracked work only:** anything that outlives one tool call starts through your harness's tracked background option (`run_in_background` on Claude Code); never start it with a trailing `&`, `nohup`, `setsid`, `disown`, or a script that detaches a process. The harness never reports on such a process, so nothing wakes you when it ends, and a turn you end to wait for it does not resume.
22	
23	**After every context compaction:** this file fits within the 20,000 characters Claude Code re-attaches, so the copy you hold is whole. A step file you read before the compaction does not survive it. Before your next action, print the board and the ledger lines the step table names (your task's and your Setup's, never the whole ledger), find your step in the table, and Read that step file in full.
24	
25	## When to Use
26	
27	```dot
28	digraph when_to_use {
29	    "Have implementation plan?" [shape=diamond];
30	    "Tasks mostly independent?" [shape=diamond];
31	    "Stay in this session?" [shape=diamond];
32	    "subagent-driven-development" [shape=box];
33	    "executing-plans" [shape=box];
34	    "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [shape=box];
35	
36	    "Have implementation plan?" -> "Tasks mostly independent?" [label="yes"];
37	    "Have implementation plan?" -> "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [label="no"];
38	    "Tasks mostly independent?" -> "Stay in this session?" [label="yes"];
39	    "Tasks mostly independent?" -> "Manual execution or brainstorm first" [label="no - tightly coupled"];
40	    "Stay in this session?" -> "subagent-driven-development" [label="yes"];
41	    "Stay in this session?" -> "executing-plans" [label="no - parallel session"];
42	}
43	```
44	
45	**vs. Executing Plans (parallel session):**
46	- Same session (no context switch)
47	- Fresh subagent per task (no context pollution)
48	- Review after each task (spec compliance + code quality), broad review at the end
49	- Faster iteration (no human-in-loop between tasks)
50	
51	## The Process
52	
53	Each step's full text is in its own file beside this one. Read a step's file when you enter the step; after a compaction, the step table below names the one to read.
54	
55	1. **Setup** ([setup.md](setup.md)): sync the state branch and find the plan's workspace, settle where the work happens (hyperpowers:using-git-worktrees), create or read the ledger and append your session line, verify, read the plan and the spec, run the pre-flight scan. Setup's last action appends `session <sid>: setup complete`.
56	2. **Take a task and dispatch** ([task-loop.md](task-loop.md)): `scripts/sdd-state next` offers a task; claim the first and switch to its branch (none to take, or blocked: post, print the board, hand back). Dispatch the implementer, answer its questions, handle its report.
57	3. **Review the task** ([review-and-complete.md](review-and-complete.md)): generate the review package and dispatch the task reviewer. Blocking findings go to step 4; a finding that conflicts with the plan text goes to your human partner first.
58	4. **Fix loop** ([fix-loop.md](fix-loop.md)): fix rounds, each with a scoped re-review, under the shared cap in the rules below. When no finding is left open, go back to review-and-complete.md for the gate.
59	5. **Codex task gate and completion** ([review-and-complete.md](review-and-complete.md)): unless the task's effective tier is low, run the per-task Codex gate (blocking findings re-enter step 4). Append the `approved` line, merge back, detach, delete the task branch, and run `scripts/sdd-state complete`; any status but `complete` stops. Then step 2.
60	6. **Final review and Finish** ([final-and-finish.md](final-and-finish.md)): when no task remains, claim the final train, dispatch the final reviewer (one fix dispatch, one scoped re-review), the decision extractor and the Codex final gate, delete the workspace, then use hyperpowers:finishing-a-development-branch.
61	
62	## After a compaction: the step table
63	
64	Print the board (`scripts/sdd-state board PLAN_FILE`) and the ledger lines of your task and your Setup (`grep -E '^(Task <N>:|session <sid>: setup complete)' <workspace>/progress.md`, leaving out `Task <N>:` when you hold no task); `scripts/sdd-dir PLAN_FILE` prints the workspace. Do not Read the whole ledger after a compaction: it grows with the plan. A row's newest line is the newest of your task's lines the table names (its branch, base, implementer identity, `report`, `review`, Codex gate round, `approved`, `merged` and `fix round` lines); a line it does not name, such as a deferred minor or the gate directory, leaves your step unchanged. Then Read the step file this table names:
65	
66	| State | Step file |
67	|---|---|
68	| no ledger in the workspace, or no `setup complete` line of this session in it | [setup.md](setup.md) |
69	| the board shows no task held by this session and a task without a completion line | [task-loop.md](task-loop.md) |
70	| the held task's newest line is its branch, base, implementer identity or `report` line | [task-loop.md](task-loop.md) |
71	| its newest line is a `review` or Codex gate line approving it, an `approved` line or a `merged` line | [review-and-complete.md](review-and-complete.md) |
72	| its newest line is a `fix round` line, or a `review` or Codex gate line with blocking findings | [fix-loop.md](fix-loop.md) |
73	| this session holds the final claim, or every task has a completion line | [final-and-finish.md](final-and-finish.md) |
74	
75	A state the table does not cover reads [task-loop.md](task-loop.md), and you record that in the ledger.
76	
77	The table reads these ledger lines, so write each one where its step says:
78	
79	- `session <sid>: setup complete`, Setup's last action;
80	- `Task <N>: report <status> <one line>`, after an implementer's report;
81	- `Task <N>: review <approved|blocking> <reviewer id> <one line>`, after a task review or scoped re-review;
82	- `Task <N>: codex gate round <R> <approved|blocking> <one line>`, after each per-task Codex gate round.
83	
84	## Rules for every step
85	
86	These hold in every step file. Where a step file and this section differ, this section governs.
87	
88	- Tasks with a `Task <N>: complete` line are DONE — do not re-dispatch them. Conversation memory does not survive compaction. After compaction, trust the ledger and `git log` over your own recollection.
89	- Dispatch implementer, task-reviewer, fix-round, re-review and final-reviewer subagents with `run_in_background: false`. Your next step always depends on the result, and a foreground call keeps your turn open, which is what an editor such as Zed shows as the session working. A background dispatch ends the turn while the subagent runs, and the editor shows the session idle.
90	- Run a covering command expected to finish within 10 minutes in the foreground, with an explicit timeout of at least its expected runtime and at most 600000 ms. A command that may run past 10 minutes is a tracked job; [task-loop.md](task-loop.md), "Waiting on subagents and long commands", gives its commands and watch budget.
91	- One implementer at a time in this session: parallel work is other sessions' (one controller per task branch); never dispatch two implementers at once here.
92	- Never fix findings yourself in the controller session — your context stays clean for coordination, and controller fixes skip review. The one exception is the de-minimis fix in [fix-loop.md](fix-loop.md).
93	- The task reviewer's blocking findings and the per-task Codex gate's blocking findings form one loop with ONE shared cap of **five rounds per task**: the gate does not run a count of its own.
94	- When round 5's re-review — or a per-task Codex gate at the spent cap — still leaves blocking findings open, stop dispatching and surface the task as BLOCKED, as [fix-loop.md](fix-loop.md) describes under the breaker.
95	
96	## Model Selection
97	
98	Match the model to the task's difficulty rather than defaulting. Two rules are
99	defaults you will get wrong by omission, so they stay here: **always specify
100	the model explicitly when dispatching a subagent** — an omitted model inherits
101	your session's, usually the most capable and most expensive — and **a mid-tier
102	model is the floor for reviewers and for implementers working from prose
103	descriptions**, whatever the schedule pressure. The cheapest tier is for
104	transcription, where the task's own text carries the complete code to write,
105	and for single-file mechanical fixes. The per-role guidance, the complexity
106	signals, and the fix-loop escalation rule are in
107	[model-selection.md](model-selection.md).
108	
109	## The waiting board
110	
111	Before you ask your human partner a question, hand back BLOCKED, meet an
112	empty frontier (`held` or `blocked`), or stop on a merge conflict, post what
113	you wait on: `scripts/sdd-state wait PLAN_FILE --session <sid> --kind
114	<question|tasks|merge|gate|handoff> [--task N] --note "<one line>"`, and put
115	the session lines of `scripts/sdd-state board PLAN_FILE` in what you write.
116	When you resume, clear it: `scripts/sdd-state wait PLAN_FILE --session <sid> --clear`.
117	The board is how your human partner finds the session that needs them among
118	several; a session that holds a claim and posts nothing shows as quiet
119	after half an hour, which is where they look for a permission prompt.
120	
121	## Risk Tiers (per-task Codex gate applicability)
122	
123	Tiers are `low`, `standard`, `high`, declared per task in the plan. A task
124	skips the per-task Codex gate only when all three hold: declared low, the
125	plan's own Codex gate actually reviewed the plan, and no escalation trigger
126	fired at any point during execution. That skip is recorded durably. An
127	unreviewed low tier — plan gate skipped, degraded, or outcome unknown —
128	executes as standard, and a task demoted that way runs the full train and
129	records NO tier-skip event. The Claude task reviewer and the final
130	whole-branch train never tier off. When any task did skip, write
131	`tier-skips.md` in this plan's workspace; Final Review hands its path to the
132	final reviewer and the final Codex gate. The escalation triggers, the
133	fallback rules, and the exact ledger line shape are in
134	[risk-tiers.md](risk-tiers.md) — read it before dispatching any task declared
135	low.
136	
137	## Common Rationalizations
138	
139	The excuses that show up mid-run and what is actually true:
140	[common-rationalizations.md](common-rationalizations.md). Read it the moment you
141	catch yourself justifying a shortcut.
142	
143	## Example Workflow
144	
145	A complete worked run, dispatch through finish:
146	[example-workflow.md](example-workflow.md).
